relevance_rank_note: Measures B1 directly and cell-free: SPR kinetics of intact lipoproteins from APOE3/E3 versus APOE3/E4 men binding immobilized LDLR ectodomain, including the dissociation rate of the stable complex, so it tests the adhesion half of H4 on a recycling receptor; B2 (receptor recycling) is never measured, and the system is plasma lipoproteins and hepatocytes rather than brain cells.

description: In SPR of fasting VLDL1-rich lipoproteins binding immobilized LDLR, particles from APOE3/E4 carriers dissociated from the stable complex more slowly than APOE3/E3 particles, so once formed the complex was more stable.
quote: the dissociation rate constant (kd2) was lower (P = 0.013) and overall K2 was higher (P = 0.032) for the second step of the binding of fasting APOE3/E4 VLDL1-rich particles to the LDLR. This indicates that once the AB* complex is formed, it is more stable and dissociates at a slower rate
summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (slower dissociation of VLDL1-LDLR complex, more stable complex)
system: Ex vivo human plasma lipoproteins: VLDL1-rich triglyceride-rich lipoprotein fraction (Svedberg flotation rate 60-400) isolated from fasting plasma of healthy men prospectively recruited as APOE3/E3 (n = 10) or APOE3/E4 (n = 11), mean age 48 years, samples pooled from two subjects per preparation; surface plasmon resonance on a BIAcore 3000 with purified LDLR ectodomain amine-coupled to a CM5 chip, lipoproteins at 5 nM apoB in HBS-N pH 7.4 with 1 mM calcium chloride at 25 degrees C, two-state binding model fit. whole circulating lipoprotein particles from APOE3/E4 heterozygote carriers binding a purified receptor ectodomain at pH 7.4 in a cell-free assay, not APOE4 protein in human brain cells, and the apoE is carried on a particle alongside apoB rather than tested as an isolated isoform.
location: Table 1, VLDL1-rich kd2 and K2 columns
human_check: Effect is N/A because the authors print only group means with SEM (kd2 11.2 +/- 0.2 versus 9.7 +/- 0.4 x 10-4 s-1) and no percent or fold change for this contrast; computing one would be a read-off. P = 0.013 is the genotype t-test for kd2; the K2 contrast in the same sentence carries P = 0.032. n = 5 is independent SPR experiments, not subjects, and each sample pools two subjects. The genotype comparison is E3/E4 heterozygotes versus E3/E3, so the E4 effect is diluted by the E3 allele. No figure was viewed.

description: In the same SPR assay, LDL isolated from APOE3/E4 subjects bound the LDLR with lower overall affinity than APOE3/E3 LDL, the opposite direction to the hypothesis for this lipoprotein fraction.
quote: This was reflected in the KA (0.5 × 109 M−1 vs. 0.7 × 109 M−1, respectively) (P = 0.019) indicating that LDL isolated from APOE3/E4 subjects had a lower binding affinity to the LDLR relative to the APOE3/E3 genotype.
summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (lower LDL binding affinity for LDLR) [against]
system: Ex vivo human plasma LDL (density 1.019-1.063 g/ml) isolated after an overnight fast from an independent group of healthy APOE3/E3 and APOE3/E4 male subjects; surface plasmon resonance on a BIAcore 3000 with purified LDLR ectodomain amine-coupled to a CM5 chip, LDL at 5 nM apoB in HBS-N pH 7.4 with 1 mM calcium chloride at 25 degrees C, two-state binding model fit. human plasma LDL, whose main LDLR ligand is apoB-100 rather than apoE, binding a purified receptor ectodomain at pH 7.4 in a cell-free assay, not APOE4 protein in human brain cells.
human_check: Against the hypothesis for the LDL fraction: E4 carriers' LDL binds LDLR less tightly, not more. Effect N/A because the authors print the two KA values but no percent or fold difference; deriving one would be a read-off. LDL uses apoB-100 as its primary LDLR ligand, so this fraction is a weaker test of apoE adhesion than the VLDL1 row, which is why relevance is set below it. No figure was viewed.

description: Co-incubating HepG2 cells with fasting triglyceride-rich lipoproteins from APOE3/E4 carriers reduced the percentage of radiolabelled LDL bound to the cell surface compared with lipoproteins from APOE3/E3 subjects, consistent with greater competition for cell-surface receptors.
quote: a significant genotype effect was observed for the percentage of 125I-LDL bound to the surface of the HepG2 cells (heparin releasable binding), with a lower percentage binding in the presence of the VLDL1-rich (P = 0.001) and VLDL2-rich (P = 0.038) fractions isolated from APOE3/E4 than APOE3/E3 individuals
summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (more competition for cell-surface LDLR, less 125I-LDL surface binding)
system: HepG2 human hepatoma cells grown to 80% confluence and held in charcoal-stripped lipoprotein-deficient serum for 48 h to upregulate surface LDLR, then incubated 5 h at 37 degrees C with 10 ug protein/ml 125I-labelled LDL alone or with 15 ug apoB/ml fasting VLDL1-rich or VLDL2-rich fraction from APOE3/E3 or APOE3/E4 men, LDL taken from the same genotype group; heparin-releasable surface-bound counts measured. immortalized human hepatoma cell line with plasma lipoproteins from APOE3/E4 heterozygotes, not human brain cells, and the readout is competition by a labelled tracer rather than apoE-receptor adhesion.
human_check: P = 0.001 belongs to the VLDL1-rich fraction named in this row; the VLDL2-rich fraction in the same sentence carries P = 0.038. Effect N/A because the authors print group means with SEM (108.2 +/- 3.5 versus 49.8 +/- 12.1 percent of the no-TRL control) but state no percent or fold difference for the genotype contrast. n is 5 independent experiments for APOE3/E3 and 4 for APOE3/E4, recorded as the paper's range rather than one end. The heparin-releasable fraction includes heparan sulphate proteoglycans and other receptors, not LDLR alone, which the authors state; so this is a surrogate, not a binding measurement. No figure was viewed.
